cities are likely to continue with their climate policies regardless of whether their state has a cap-and-trade program, that cities have other motivations for their climate policies besides the desire to reduce emissions, and that cities do not seem to be concerned about crowding out.

(i) the existence of a state-level cap-and trade program does not crowd out cities' efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions; (ii) the presence of a state-level policy does not change cities' motivations for reducing emissions; (iii) cities are motivated to reduce emissions for reasons other than the global environment.
